Filter observations by target label(s)

Source: R/PipeOpTargetLabelFilter.R
PipeOpTargetLabelFilter.Rd

PipeOpTargetLabelFilter filters the input Task by its target column and forwards the filtered Task. It is a dedicated, composable row filter that replaces ad-hoc filtering inside other PipeOps.

Filtering is applied only during training. Prediction passes every row through, regardless of whether target values are available.

Value

A PipeOpTargetLabelFilter.

Details

Target-Label Filter

After filtering, if the target is a factor:

  • For invert = FALSE the target's level set is the union of labels with their original order preserved (unobserved labels are allowed).

  • For invert = TRUE the target's level set is setdiff(original_levels, labels).

  • If this level set has fewer than two levels, it is padded with additional level(s) from the original levels (as needed) so that length(levels(target)) >= 2.

Some learners still require two observed classes in the training data; this PipeOp only guarantees the metadata (level set), not the label balance.

For a TaskClassif, the "twoclass"/"multiclass" property is updated to the new target level set, so that, e.g., a three-class task filtered to two labels can be passed to learners that only support binary tasks. With mlr3 < 1.7.0 this update is only possible when every level of the new target level set is observed in the retained rows; a padded level set with unobserved levels then keeps the property of the input task. The target of prediction tasks is left unchanged, so such a learner can only predict tasks whose target has two levels.

With drop_unused_levels = TRUE, the levels of every factor feature column are reduced to those observed in the retained training rows; target columns are never touched, so the padded target level set is kept. The resulting level sets are stored in the state and applied to the same columns at prediction, so training and prediction tasks share the same column information for downstream learners. As in mlr3pipelines::PipeOpFixFactors, prediction values of levels that were not observed in the training rows become NA. Factor columns without a feature role, such as a site column read by PipeOpSiteCorrection or group and stratum columns, are left unchanged, so later PipeOps still see their original values (e.g., the labels of unseen sites). Set drop_unused_levels = FALSE to keep all levels unchanged.

Parameters

Hyperparameters are defined in the object's param_set and can be set via param_vals.

  • labels: vector or NULL. Target label(s) used for filtering. If invert = FALSE (default), rows with target %in% labels are kept. If invert = TRUE, rows with target %in% labels are dropped. If NULL, the task is passed through unchanged.

  • target: character(1) or NULL. Name of the target column. Defaults to the task's first target via task$target_names[1].

  • invert: logical(1). If TRUE, invert the selection.

  • drop_unused_levels: logical(1). If TRUE (default), drop unused factor levels on factor feature columns after filtering and re-apply these training level sets at prediction (see Details). The target's level set is controlled explicitly.

  • drop_stratum: logical(1). If TRUE (default FALSE), remove the "stratum" role from columns that are neither features nor targets.

See also

Other PipeOps: PipeOpMBsPLS, PipeOpSiteCorrection
